chosen_type.definition: A period of seven days.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's 'DayOfWeek' is for a single day, not a week. 'Schedule' is for repeating periods. A new type is needed for a specific calendar week as an entity.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

types.embedding_query_text: FootballMatchGroup: A collection of football matches, often related by stage or timing. Also called SoccerMatchGroup, SeriesOfMatches, SetOfGames. Examples: two brilliant quarterfinals.

chosen_type.label: Series
chosen_type.justification: A 'FootballMatchGroup' is a collection of related matches. 'Series' is a general type for a group of related items forming a collection, which fits the description of 'two brilliant quarterfinals'.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Principle. Examples: soccer’s popularity.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates adequately represent an abstract 'Concept' like 'soccer’s popularity'. 'Thing' is too generic, and 'Claim'/'Statement' are specific creative works. A new type is needed for abstract ideas.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Status: The current state or condition of something. Also called Condition, State, Situation. Examples: all-time high.

chosen_type.label: StatusEnumeration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Status' refers to the current state or condition of something. 'StatusEnumeration' is a general type for various status types or states, which aligns with 'all-time high' as a state.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: IncentiveStatus
candidates.comment: IncentiveStatus is an enumeration describing the current status of an incentive, such as whether it is active or expired. Also called incentive state, benefit status, program condition. Examples: 'Active', 'Expired', 'Pending', 'Suspended'.

types.embedding_query_text: Attribute: A quality or characteristic belonging to a person, place, or thing. Also called Characteristic, Quality, Feature. Examples: work ethic and mentality, lack of quality on the ball.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: An 'Attribute' is a quality or characteristic, which is directly represented by the schema.org 'Property' type, used to indicate attributes of a 'Thing'. The mentions are abstract qualities.

mentions: lack of quality on the ball

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

types.embedding_query_text: Environment: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates. Also called Setting, Surroundings, Context. Examples: positive environment.

chosen_type.label: ContextualEnvironment
chosen_type.definition: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates.
chosen_type.justification: While 'Place' is a physical location, 'Environment' as in 'positive environment' refers more to abstract conditions or circumstances. A new type is needed to capture this contextual meaning.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Trip
candidates.comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

types.embedding_query_text: Quality: A distinctive attribute or characteristic possessed by someone or something. Also called Trait, Feature, Property. Examples: real promise.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: A 'Quality' is a distinctive attribute or characteristic, which is directly represented by the schema.org 'Property' type, used to indicate attributes of a 'Thing'. 'real promise' is an abstract quality.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

types.embedding_query_text: Trait: A distinguishing quality or characteristic, typically one belonging to a person. Also called Characteristic, Attribute, Feature. Examples: Ego, personality.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: A 'Trait' is a distinguishing quality or characteristic, which is directly represented by the schema.org 'Property' type, used to indicate attributes of a 'Thing'. 'Ego' and 'personality' are abstract traits.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Medal, Trophy. Examples: World Cup title, World Cup winner’s medal.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A prize or honor bestowed for achievement.
chosen_type.justification: An 'Award' is a type of 'Grant' (a transfer of something) given for achievement. 'MonetaryGrant' is too specific, and other candidates are events or actions. A new type is needed for the general concept of an award.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalCondition: A state of health that deviates from the normal, often requiring medical attention. Also called Illness, Sickness, Ailment, Disease. Examples: injury.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'MedicalCondition' type is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE and its definition, explicitly including 'injuries' as a type of medical condition.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValueType: A category or type of financial cost or payment. Also called FeeType, CostCategory, PaymentType. Examples: club fees.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryCostType
chosen_type.definition: A category or type of financial cost or payment.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a 'type' or 'category' of monetary value or payment. 'MonetaryAmount' is the value itself. A new type is needed for the classification of costs.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: PaymentMethodType
candidates.comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: PaymentStatusType
candidates.comment: PaymentStatusType is an enumeration for specific payment statuses. Also called payment state, transaction status, billing status. Examples: PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, PaymentDeclined, PaymentFailed. Distinct from OrderStatus, which describes the overall order state.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

types.embedding_query_text: CareerType: A classification or description of a professional path or occupation. Also called JobType, ProfessionCategory, OccupationalField. Examples: competitive soccer careers.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: A 'CareerType' is a classification of a professional path or occupation, which aligns well with the schema.org 'Occupation' type, representing a profession or job.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

types.embedding_query_text: SportCategory: A classification or grouping of different sports. Also called SportType, AthleticCategory. Examples: youth sports.

chosen_type.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
chosen_type.justification: A 'SportCategory' is a classification or grouping of sports, which is directly represented by 'PhysicalActivityCategory' as an enumeration for categories of physical activity.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

types.embedding_query_text: Strategy: A plan of action or policy designed to achieve a major or overall aim. Also called Approach, Method, Plan. Examples: specialization.

chosen_type.label: Plan
chosen_type.definition: A plan of action or policy designed to achieve a major or overall aim.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Strategy' refers to the plan itself, not the action of planning ('PlanAction'). 'Specialty' is an area of expertise. A new type is needed for the concept of a plan or strategy.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: PlanAction
candidates.comment: PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging. Examples: planning a wedding, scheduling a meeting, arranging a trip itinerary, setting up a project timeline.

candidates.label: ScheduleAction
candidates.comment: The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking. Examples: scheduling a doctor's appointment, booking a meeting room, planning a project timeline, arranging a delivery. Distinct from ReserveAction, which implies making a reservation for a specific resource or service.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

candidates.label: ExercisePlan
candidates.comment: An ExercisePlan is a CreativeWork representing a fitness-related activity designed for a specific health purpose, including routines or clinician-prescribed activities. Also called workout plan, fitness regimen, training program. Examples: A 30-day weight loss plan, a physical therapy exercise routine, a marathon training schedule, a yoga sequence.

types.embedding_query_text: Pathway: A course of action or a route to achieve something. Also called Route, Course, Direction. Examples: participation pathway, performance pathway.

chosen_type.label: Course
chosen_type.justification: A 'Pathway' as a 'course of action or a route to achieve something' aligns well with the schema.org 'Course' type, which describes an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge or ability.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: TravelAction
candidates.comment: The act of moving from a starting location to a destination using a specified mode of transport. Also called journey, commute, voyage. Examples: traveling by car from home to work, flying from New York to London, taking a bus to another city.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

candidates.label: TieAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.

types.embedding_query_text: Narrative: A spoken or written account of connected events; a story. Also called Story, Account, Tale. Examples: unfounded yet ongoing narrative.

chosen_type.label: ShortStory
chosen_type.justification: A 'Narrative' is a spoken or written account of connected events. 'ShortStory' explicitly includes 'narrative' in its definition and is a type of creative work that tells a story.

candidates.label: Audiobook
candidates.comment: An Audiobook is an AudioObject that is a spoken-word recording of a book or other text. Also called spoken book, recorded book, audio novel. Examples: a narrated version of "Moby Dick", a recorded lecture series, a podcast adaptation of a novel. Distinct from Book, which is the written text itself.

candidates.label: AmpStory
candidates.comment: An AmpStory is a CreativeWork with a visual storytelling format designed for online viewing, especially on mobile devices. Also called AMP Web Story, visual story, mobile story. Examples: A Google AMP Story about a travel destination, a news publisher's visual story, a brand's product showcase story.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: ShortStory
candidates.comment: A brief work of literature, typically written in narrative prose, focusing on a single plot or theme. Also called tale, novelette, short fiction, narrative. Examples: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Tell-Tale Heart', O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi', a story from a literary magazine.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Function, Position, Capacity. Examples: officials, co-host.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Role' type is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE and its definition, representing a function or part played by a person or thing.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.embedding_query_text: Sport: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment. Also called Athletics, Game, PhysicalActivity. Examples: soccer.

chosen_type.label: Sport
chosen_type.definition: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org lacks a direct type for 'Sport' as the activity itself. Existing sport-related types are for events, teams, or organizations. A new type is needed for the abstract concept of a sport.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

types.embedding_query_text: Context: The circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea, and in terms of which it can be fully understood and assessed. Also called Setting, Background, Environment. Examples: international stage.

chosen_type.label: Context
chosen_type.definition: The circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea, and in terms of which it can be fully understood and assessed.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent 'Context' as an abstract concept or setting. 'Place' is too concrete, and 'BackgroundNewsArticle' provides context but isn't the context itself. A new type is needed.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Level: A position on a scale of amount, quantity, extent, or quality. Also called Standard, Degree, Rank. Examples: professional level.

chosen_type.label: MemberProgramTier
chosen_type.justification: A 'Level' refers to a position on a scale. 'MemberProgramTier' explicitly uses 'level' and 'tier' to describe a position or status within a program, which is the closest conceptual fit among the candidates for 'professional level'.

candidates.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the level of evidence supporting a medical guideline. Also called evidence strength, guideline reliability, data quality level. Examples: "Level A evidence", "Grade 1 recommendation", "strong evidence".

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.embedding_query_text: GoalDescription Examples: absolute worldie.

chosen_type.label: SportsGoalDescription
chosen_type.definition: A descriptive term for a goal scored in a sports match.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates fit 'GoalDescription' as a descriptive term for a goal. It is a form of creative expression or commentary. 'CreativeWork' is a suitable parent for such a description.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: SizeSpecification
candidates.comment: Properties related to a product's size, including a size code, system, group, and measurements. Also called product dimensions, sizing details, garment measurements, fit specifications. Examples: a shirt with size 'M' (Medium) in 'US' size system, a shoe with 'EU 42' size, a dress with 'Petite' size group.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: A MeasurementTypeEnumeration listing various dimensions of a person's body, often used for clothing fit. Also called body dimension type, clothing size measurement, anthropometric measurement. Examples: "Chest circumference", "Waist size", "Inseam length", "Shoe size".

types.embedding_query_text: Title Examples: defending champion.

chosen_type.label: Designation
chosen_type.definition: A name, title, or status given to someone or something.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Title' refers to a status or designation, such as 'defending champion'. None of the candidates represent this meaning. A new type is needed for such a designation.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.
